title: Determination, reinterpretation, valuation: the three typed operations
subject: typed-operations
ratio:
Every interpretive act recorded in the registry is typed as exactly one of three operations,
structurally separate: `determination` (the publish-time recorded choice, at the author's own
authority tier, of what binds -- realist terminology, since the interpreter chooses rather than
merely recognizes a pre-existing meaning), `reinterpretation` (a later act stating what a
previously determined ratio means: `declarative` when it fixes an indeterminate ratio for a new
case, `corrective-restrictive` or `corrective-extensive` when it argues the originally identified
ratio was merely apparent and states a narrower or wider real ratio), and `valuation` (a
metatextual act that changes a ratio's institutional force -- declaring a passage `obiter`,
`error-in-pronouncement`, or `context-change` -- without touching its meaning). The `operation`
field is mandatory on every record, exhaustive at these three types and their per-type subtype
enums, and defaults to `{"type": "determination", "subtype": null}` when a publish supplies none.
Conflict detection and the overruling protocol branch on this typing: a record may never carry an
untyped "precedent" blob conflating identification, reinterpretation, and valuation, because doing
so makes disagreement about which of the three happened unadjudicable.
scope_conditions: any agent publishing to the registry
the operation field, its type and subtype enums
revisit_trigger: Revisit if the operation taxonomy gains or loses a type or subtype via a recorded amendment
validity_conditions: the registry CLI enforces the operation matrix at publish
